proposals.evidence: DEDR3647: Tamil nām, Malayalam nām and Tulu nama occur in the inclusive we family. Pattapu namu preserves the n-m stem with short vowels and final u; its source explicitly distinguishes this inclusive response from naŋgu exclusive. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR3688: Kodagu niŋga and Tamil nīṅkaḷ occur in the plural you family. Pattapu nēŋgu preserves the nasal-velar formation with a different long vowel and final u. Its source only says you, so plurality is inferred from the comparison and contrasted singular niyi responses, not silently added to the gloss. Whole-article family membership is proposed; inheritance versus local transmission remains subject to review. proposals.evidence: DEDR5297: Tamil/Malayalam vaḻi and Kannada baḻi denote way, path or road. Pattapu voli is proposed with a rounded first vowel and plain lateral retained. proposals.evidence: DEDR1254: Tamil kayiṟu and Malayalam kayaṟu denote rope; Kodagu kē·rï shows a shorter vocalic formation. Pattapu kaʷɹu retains initial k and the rhotic with final u, but its superscript rounded glide differs from the Tamil/Malayalam medial sequence. This is a qualified family comparison, not a claimed exact sound match or transcription correction.
